newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity hires Bankers as index funds adviser.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity hires Bankers as index funds adviser.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Thursday it has hired Bankers Trust New York Corp to sub-advise its planned six equity index mutual funds.
But Fidelity added that it still expects to lose money on the funds for the next couple of years.

Bankers Trust will sub-advise Fidelity's three new equity index funds, to be introduced this fall, and the three current equity index funds, pending shareholder approval, said Robert Pozen, head of Fidelity's mutual fund division Fidelity Management & Research.
In order to offer competitive prices, Fidelity will until the end of 1999 charge its customers a fee lower than the advisory fee it will pay Bankers Trust, Pozen told reporters in a conference call.

"We are subsidizing these funds," he said. "We offer them because our customers want them. In the long-term, we need to bring down our cost structure so that we can offer them at a good price to our customers and come out reasonably ourselves."
After 1999, Fidelity will raise the fees to more profitable rates, but remain at competitive levels, he said.
"Our goal is to get to the point where we will break even and make a modest profit," Pozen said.

Bankers Trust, because of its size and expertise, can handle much of the custodial and other operations for the funds at a lower cost than Fidelity could and allows the fund company to offer customers lower rates, he said.
"We're not geared up to do index managing," he said. "They can do the thing much more cost-effectively and more cost-efficiently then we can," Pozen said.

Fidelity has guaranteed on its Spartan Market Index Fund and its Spartan U.S. Equity Index Fund, which track the Standard & Poor's 500 index, an expense ratio of 19 basis points until the end of 1999.
Vanguard Group charges an expense ratio of 20 basis points for its popular domestic equity index funds, which are run at cost and are not subsidized, a spokesman said.

In addition to expense ratios, mutual fund companies also charge transaction fees, which can vary according to the efficiency of the company. Vanguard's index funds have had lower fees than Fidelity's recently, said Vanguard spokesman Brian Mattes.
Fidelity has capped the rates on its other domestic equity index fund and on the proposed three new index funds, Pozen said.

Fidelity plans to introduce the Spartan Total Market Index Fund, which will track the Wilshire 5000 index, the Spartan Extended Market Index Fund, tracking the Wilshire 4500 index, and the Spartan International Index Fund, which tracks the EAFE index, later this fall.
Pozen said Fidelity has no plans to hire a sub-advisor for its other mutual funds.
